neighbours.label: a quantity or kind noun that heads an 'of' phrase (a number of, an amount of, a great deal of, this kind of, the type of)
fire: Researchers have raised a number of concerns about the drug.
Only a tiny amount of salt is needed for the sauce.
The project required a great deal of patience from everyone.
Farmers rarely see this kind of weather in April.
The museum avoids the type of crowds seen in summer.
Visitors brought a large number of gifts for the children.
She spent a fair amount of time fixing the old car.
He asked what sort of training the job would need.
quiet: Researchers have raised concerns about the drug.
Only salt is needed for the sauce.
The project required patience from everyone.
Farmers rarely see snow in April.
The museum avoids crowds in summer.
Visitors wrote the number on a card for the children.
She spent the morning fixing the old car.
He asked what training the job would need.

predictions: Fires on number/amount/deal/kind/type/set when followed by 'of' + plural/mass noun; quiet on the same nouns used literally and on sentences with the quantifier removed.
notes: Probe: 'a number of toxins' 0.36, 'small amount of' 0.32, 'great deal of' 0.40, 'this kind of' 0.28, 'the type of' 0.41; without the quantifier 0.007 and 0.000; literal 'The number on the door' 0.035.
